subject.title: Feature: browser tool - expose CDP Network domain for request interception

question: Should OpenClaw expose model-facing browser network request listing/body/interception, and what redaction, permission, profile-support, and interception-vs-observation contract should it use?
rationale: The requested feature changes what authenticated browser traffic the model can see or affect, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security boundary or product contract.

options.title: Design A Safe Browser-Plugin Contract
options.body: Define a bounded Browser plugin API for request listing, response-body access, and any active interception with explicit redaction, profile support, output wrapping, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Diagnostics-Only First
options.body: Expose only passive request listing and bounded response-body retrieval to the model first, and defer active request mutation/interception until the security model is proven.

options.title: Defer Model-Facing Network Access
options.body: Keep current CLI/control diagnostics only and decline model-facing network access until there is a stronger product/security reason.

recommendation.title: Design A Safe Browser-Plugin Contract
recommendation.body: Define a bounded Browser plugin API for request listing, response-body access, and any active interception with explicit redaction, profile support, output wrapping, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the browser plugin model-facing tool schema, dispatcher, and route ownership boundary.
